staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this exact vulnerable checkout, and the line anchors below are grounded in that tree.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42490490 (glib): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target fuzz_date_parse [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42490490
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the one-byte file `0xfd`. `fuzz_date_parse` duplicates it with `g_strndup()` into a 2-byte heap string `fd 00` and passes that NUL-terminated buffer to `g_date_set_parse()`. Vulnerable `g_date_set_parse()` never checks that `str` is valid UTF-8 before calling `g_date_prepare_to_parse()`, even though the date parser later uses UTF-8 iteration helpers that require valid input. In `g_date_fill_parse_tokens()`, the `0xfd` byte yields no decimal fields, so `pt->num_ints == 0` and the `< 3 integers` branch calls `g_utf8_casefold (str, -1)` on the original invalid string. Inside `g_utf8_casefold()`, `g_utf8_next_char(p)` treats the leading byte `0xfd` as a 6-byte UTF-8 leader and advances `p` from the 2-byte allocation to `str + 6`; the next loop test then dereferences `*p` there and AddressSanitizer reports a heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 at `glib/guniprop.c:1170`. The staged patch fixes the bug by adding `if (!g_utf8_validate (str, -1, NULL)) return;` in `g_date_set_parse()` before parsing begins.

source.description: First non-harness project statement that consumes the attacker-controlled NUL-terminated string by entering GLib's date parser.
source.value_from: The staged witness at `gt_results/arvo_42490490/poc` is exactly one byte `0xfd` (sha256 `3e151409ace91cb3394fecd59e92b5dc42c0aad29993a1858f2f70a0866a539b`). Harness line `fuzzing/fuzz_date_parse.c:12` duplicates that byte with `g_strndup ((const gchar *) data, size)`, so this call receives the exact 2-byte heap string `fd 00` that ASan later identifies as region `[0x602000000070,0x602000000072)`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The next loop-condition dereference `*p` reads from the pointer already advanced beyond the 2-byte `fd 00` heap string.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 1` at `glib/guniprop.c:1170:40` on address `0x602000000076`, which is 4 bytes to the right of the 2-byte region `[0x602000000070,0x602000000072)` allocated for the duplicated input string.

root_cause.description: Source and root cause. `g_date_set_parse()` forwards `str` into UTF-8-sensitive parsing without first rejecting invalid UTF-8.
root_cause.note: The staged patch inserts `if (!g_utf8_validate (str, -1, NULL)) return;` immediately before this call, expressing the missing obligation that the vulnerable source omitted.

tainted_value_origin.code: nul_terminated_data = (unsigned char *) g_strndup ((const gchar *) data, size);
tainted_value_origin.description: The one-byte witness is materialized here into the exact heap string later consumed by `g_date_set_parse()`: `g_strndup()` allocates `size + 1 == 2` bytes, copies `0xfd`, and appends `\0`.

parser_admitted.description: The fuzz harness has already crossed its unscored boundary and entered GLib's date parser with the NUL-terminated heap string `fd 00`. The saved crash stack `g_date_set_parse -> g_date_prepare_to_parse -> g_date_fill_parse_tokens -> g_utf8_casefold` confirms this shallow parser path.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness duplicates the exact one-byte witness `0xfd` with `g_strndup()` into a 2-byte heap string `fd 00` and passes that NUL-terminated buffer to `g_date_set_parse()`.
`g_date_set_parse()` forwards the duplicated string into `g_date_prepare_to_parse()` without the UTF-8 validation guard added by the fix.
The parser extracts no decimal fields from the `0xfd` byte, so `pt->num_ints == 0` and the `< 3 integers` branch casefolds the original string as UTF-8.

`g_utf8_next_char()` advances past the 2-byte `fd 00` allocation as though `0xfd` started a 6-byte UTF-8 character, and the next loop test reads `*p` out of bounds, matching the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.code:
nul_terminated_data = (unsigned char *) g_strndup ((const gchar *) data, size);
g_date_set_parse (date, (const gchar *) nul_terminated_data);
fine_trace.note: The harness duplicates the exact one-byte witness `0xfd` with `g_strndup()`, which allocates `size + 1 == 2` bytes and appends `\0`. The library therefore receives the heap string `fd 00`, matching ASan's 2-byte allocation context.

Source and root cause. `g_date_set_parse()` consumes the NUL-terminated string from step 0 and enters GLib's date parser without first checking `g_utf8_validate (str, -1, NULL)`. The fix adds that early-return guard immediately before this call.

With `str == {0xfd, 0x00}`, the first byte is nonzero but not an ASCII digit, so the inner digit loop never records a number. The outer scan advances `s` once to the terminator and exits with `pt->num_ints == 0`.
Because step 2 left `pt->num_ints == 0`, the parser takes the month-name path. That path is only reached when fewer than three numeric fields were extracted.

The `< 3 integers` branch casefolds the original `fd 00` string as NUL-terminated UTF-8 (`len == -1`). Because step 1 never rejected invalid UTF-8, this call hands the invalid lead byte directly to UTF-8 iteration code.

On the first loop iteration, `p` still points at the lead byte `0xfd`. `g_utf8_next_char()` is the macro `p + g_utf8_skip[*p]`, and GLib documents it as requiring valid UTF-8; for `0xfd`, `g_utf8_skip[*p] == 6`, so `p` becomes `str + 6`, four bytes past the 2-byte `fd 00` allocation.

Sink. After step 5 advanced `p` to `str + 6`, the next loop test reevaluates `*p`. Because `len == -1`, the left side of the `&&` is true, so the condition dereferences the out-of-bounds pointer and performs the 1-byte read that ASan reports at `0x602000000076`, 4 bytes to the right of the 2-byte region `[0x602000000070,0x602000000072)`.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The sink is the exact top project frame in the saved ASan trace: the `*p` read in `g_utf8_casefold()` at `glib/guniprop.c:1170`.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Not directly. The allocation context only creates the 2-byte `fd 00` heap string, while the patchable bug is `g_date_set_parse()` forwarding that string without the UTF-8 validation that the fix adds.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack is `g_utf8_casefold -> g_date_fill_parse_tokens -> g_date_prepare_to_parse -> g_date_set_parse -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, which matches the fine trace's parser entry, no-digit branch, casefold call, pointer advance, and sink.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The exact witness byte `0xfd` becomes the `fd 00` heap string in step 0, is forwarded unvalidated into `g_date_set_parse()` at step 1, leaves `pt->num_ints == 0` at step 2, reaches `g_utf8_casefold (str, -1)` at step 4, and then makes `g_utf8_next_char()` advance `p` to `str + 6` before the step-6 out-of-bounds `*p` read.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the issue by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42490490 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which produced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` and `READ of size 1` in `g_utf8_casefold` with stack `g_utf8_casefold -> g_date_fill_parse_tokens -> g_date_prepare_to_parse -> g_date_set_parse -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.

format.name: raw g_date_set_parse witness string
format.contract: Exactly the witness stored at `gt_results/arvo_42490490/poc` (1 byte, sha256 `3e151409ace91cb3394fecd59e92b5dc42c0aad29993a1858f2f70a0866a539b`): a single byte `0xfd`. `fuzz_date_parse` duplicates it with `g_strndup()` into the 2-byte heap string `fd 00` before calling `g_date_set_parse()`. The staged artifacts justify this exact invalid-UTF-8 witness and the missing UTF-8 validation fixed by the patch; they do not prove a broader trigger contract beyond the saved witness.
